parole.testo: Uncertain. Compare Sanskrit ब्रध्न (bradhnà, “reddish, yellow”), Proto-Slavic *bro(d)nъ (“colored”), perhaps pointing to Proto-Indo-European *bʰredʰ-n/m- and therefore Proto-Albanian *bradma, though these cognates have had other proposed etymologies.

parole.significato: the first and last three days of March
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes (“three”), with the initial dh- probably deriving from an original compound (cf. dhjetë), from earlier *ndrim, from Proto-Albanian *ən-treima.

parole.significato: to gather, gather in or up
parole.testo: From older mbëledh, from Old Albanian ënbëljedh, made of a prefix ënbë- of disputed origin + a component ljedh from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to gather”) (compare Latin legere, Ancient Greek λέγω (légō)). A compound *ne + *-s, from Proto-Indo-European *nō kwe. From Proto-Albanian *(e)nō ̊, from Proto-Indo-European *(h1)nē̆-, *(h1)nō̆- (“after, behind, next to/after”). Cognate to Ancient Greek ἔνη(ς) (énē(s)), ἔνας (énas, “the day after tomorrow”) and Gothic 𐌽𐌴𐍈 (nēƕ, “after”).
Orel derives the prefix from the same root as ith (“behind”), namely Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰs, through Proto-Albanian *eś-.
